title: Ports and Protocols: The Complete Beginner's Guide

scenes.narration: A big office building has one main phone number. Every department has its own extension. Ports are those extensions.

scenes.heading: Office extensions
scenes.narration: An I P address is the main number. The port number tells the call which department to reach. The first group, up to one thousand twenty three, are well known. The middle group, up to forty nine thousand, are registered. The rest are dynamic, picked by your computer for each chat.

scenes.heading: The big ones
scenes.narration: Learn these by heart. Web uses eighty and four four three. S S H is twenty two, and Telnet is twenty three. Mail uses twenty five, one ten and one forty three. D N S is fifty three, and D H C P uses sixty seven and sixty eight.

scenes.heading: Common mix-ups
scenes.narration: Three tips. U D P uses ports as well. Telnet is twenty three, not twenty two. D N S uses T C P for zone transfers.

items.wrong: Port numbers are only for TCP

scenes.heading: Remember this
scenes.narration: So, to recap. A port number picks the application. Memorise the common ones: twenty two, twenty five, fifty three, eighty and four four three. Ports range from zero to sixty five thousand. Ready to practise? Try the Courseiva ports lab.
